beats.say: A famous professor climbed a mountain to meet a Zen master. He had not come to listen. He had come to talk.
The master smiled and began to pour the tea. The cup filled up... and still he kept pouring.
Stop, cried the professor. It is full! No more will go in. Exactly, said the master. Like this cup, you are full of your opinions.
How can I show you anything, unless you first empty your cup? Tonight, put down everything you know. One breath. Empty. Only this.
Two monks came to a flooded river. A young woman stood on the bank, afraid of the current. And monks were not allowed even to look at a woman.
The old monk simply lifted her up, carried her through the water, and set her down on the far side. Then the two of them walked on.
For hours the young monk burned in silence. At last he exploded: How could you touch her? And the old monk said: I left her at the river. You are still carrying her.
Who are you still carrying? Put them down. Feel how light you are.
A man asked a Zen master: Where is this truth you keep talking about? The master said nothing. He just raised his finger, and pointed at the full moon.
The man stared at the finger. What a finger, he said. Let me bow to this finger. Let me build a temple for this finger.
And the master laughed. Fool, he said. Look where it is pointing. All the books, all the temples... they are only fingers.
Don't hold on to the finger. Lift your eyes. Tonight, look at the moon, and say nothing.
A girl in the village became pregnant, and to protect the real father she named the old master, Hakuin. Her family came to his hut, screaming insults.
Hakuin listened, and said only: Is that so? When the baby was born, they left it with him. He cared for it with great love, while the whole village turned against him.
A year later the girl confessed. Her family came back, ashamed, begging forgiveness, asking for the child. Hakuin handed the baby back and said: Is that so?
Praise and blame are only weather. Be the sky. The next time someone judges you, smile inside, and say: Is that so?
A farmer's only horse ran away. Such bad luck, said the neighbours. Maybe, said the farmer. A week later it came back with seven wild horses. Such good luck! Maybe.
His son tried to ride one, fell, and broke his leg. Bad luck! said the neighbours. And the farmer only said: maybe.
Then the army came to take every young man to the war. They left the boy with the broken leg behind. Good luck! Maybe.
You never know where the story is going. Don't close the book after one page. Whatever happens today, try one word: maybe.
One night Mulla Nasruddin was on his knees under a street lamp, searching. A neighbour asked: What have you lost, Mulla? My key, he said.
So the neighbour got down and searched with him, for a long, long time. Finally he asked: Are you sure you lost it here? No, said Nasruddin. I lost it in my house.
Then why are we searching out here? Because, said Nasruddin, there is more light here!
We laugh. But we all search outside for what we lost inside. Tonight, turn the lamp around. Close your eyes, and look in.
Mulla Nasruddin came galloping through the bazaar on his donkey, shouting: Has anyone seen my donkey? I have lost my donkey!
He searched every street. People were laughing so hard they could not speak. At last an old man shouted: Mulla, you are sitting on it!
Nasruddin looked down, amazed. Thank God, he said. I was so worried!
You are searching for peace, for joy, for God. Stop for one moment. Look down. You may be sitting on it.
In a Himalayan forest a little deer smelled the most beautiful fragrance in the world. Musk. And it went mad, searching for where it came from.
It ran through the forest, over the rocks, through the streams. Day and night, without food, without sleep. The smell was always there, just ahead.
It never found it. Because the musk was inside its own body. It was carrying the very thing it was chasing.
What you are chasing is not out there. Stop running, just for a moment. Breathe in. Smell it. It is you.
A man is rowing over a misty river when another boat crashes into his. He jumps up, furious, ready to shout and fight.
Then he looks. The other boat is empty. It came loose from its rope and drifted down the river. And all his anger is suddenly gone.
Chuang Tzu says: empty your own boat as you go down the river of life, and nobody will fight you. There will be nobody there to hurt.
When someone pushes you today, feel for that empty boat inside. Let the insult pass through you, like wind.
A proud samurai demanded of an old monk: Tell me about heaven and hell! The monk looked at him and said: You? You are too stupid to understand.
The samurai went red with rage, and pulled out his sword to cut him down. And quietly the monk said: That is hell.
The samurai froze. He understood. He put the sword away and bowed, full of gratitude. And the monk said: That is heaven.
Heaven and hell are not far away. You step into one of them every time you react. Watch for the next one coming.
